ai.title: Add scripts package for fine-tuning dataset generation
ai.summary: New scripts package with generate-fine-tuning-dataset.ts. Builds Claude fine-tuning data from git diffs. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Outputs tmp/ dataset.

eli5.text: The team added a new set of helper tools that can study how the project's code changed over its past thousand updates. When a developer runs the tool, it looks at the before-and-after versions of files, asks an AI assistant to explain each change in plain language, and saves the results into a temporary folder to build a training dataset. This only affects developers working on the project's internal scripts, and they would notice it by seeing new folders and instructions appearing in their local development environment after pulling the latest changes.

Each JSONL entry contains a messages array with a user prompt embedding oldFile and claudeSketch, and an assistant response containing the patch. eli5.text: When the team's internal tool builds examples of code-writing conversations to train the assistant, it now also saves those examples in a new file alongside the existing one, so the assistant can learn from them in a format it can read more easily. While doing this, it also pulls in fewer past examples (down from a thousand to a hundred) and looks at fewer files per example (down from a hundred to ten), which means it spends less time gathering data but finishes faster. Since this is internal tooling used only by the development team and not by anyone outside the company, you as an external user wouldn't notice this change when using the product.

eli5.text: The dataset builder now reads from a list of projects instead of one fixed folder, so it can pull code samples from both Manifold and Litestar in the same run. Each project gets its own labeled output file, and the helper that shuffles the samples now comes from a standard utility library added to the project. If you looked now, you'd see separate dataset files named after each project appearing in the output instead of one generic file.

ai.title: Expand file types and scale dataset generation
ai.summary: Updated scripts/generate-fine-tuning-dataset.ts to include Python, JS, Java, Go, C/C++, Rust, and Markdown files alongside TypeScript. Increased commit scan to 1000 and parallel processes to 20. Added logic to skip diffs with fewer than 10 changed lines.

eli5.text: The system that builds training examples for the assistant now looks at many more code files (Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, C/C++, Rust, and Markdown, not just TypeScript) and scans ten times as many recent code changes. You won't notice this directly, but it means the assistant's training data covers a much broader range of programming languages and real-world edits. Only changes that modify at least 10 lines are included, and the system now processes these examples in larger parallel batches, making the dataset generation faster and more thorough.

ai.title: Add blacklist filter to fine-tuning dataset generator
ai.summary: scripts/generate-fine-tuning-dataset.ts now skips files containing 'This file was automatically generated' via BLACK_LIST_STRINGS. FILES_TO_PROCESS reduced from 100 to 20. libgdx mock project added to PROJECTS_LIST.

eli5.text: If you looked at the dataset generator today, you would notice it now silently skips any file containing the phrase 'This file was automatically generated', so mock or boilerplate files no longer pollute the sample pool. The tool still pulls code from the same projects, but it processes only 20 files at a time instead of 100, making each run smaller and faster. You would also see a fourth project, named libgdx, appear in its list of codebases it scans for examples. These adjustments are already live in the internal script, so anyone running it will get cleaner, narrower results right away.

ai.title: Normalize line endings in fine-tuning dataset generation
ai.summary: Added `.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n')` to `oldContent`, `newContent`, and `patch` in `scripts/generate-fine-tuning-dataset.ts`. This ensures consistent Unix-style line endings in the generated dataset, preventing potential parsing or model training issues caused by Windows-style CRLF sequences.

eli5.text: When the assistant builds a training dataset from code changes, it now cleans up invisible line-ending characters that can sneak in when files are edited on Windows computers. The cleanup makes all line breaks uniform before the data is saved, so the training examples won't accidentally contain mixed formats that could confuse or slow down the learning process. You wouldn't see a difference in the code itself, but the dataset the assistant uses to learn will be neater and more consistent.

When true, skips Helicone baseURL and auth headers, routing directly to Anthropic. Used by scripts/generate-fine-tuning-dataset.ts to bypass proxy for dataset generation. Dataset entries now include filePath and old file line numbers in prompts.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the system that generates example code for the AI can now choose to send its requests directly to Anthropic instead of always routing them through a middle-layer service called Helicone. The dataset-generation script (used internally to build AI training data) now uses this direct path, which lets it bypass that middle layer for simpler, faster runs. The prompts it creates also now include the source file path and original line numbers, so the AI better understands where code changes are coming from.

ai.title: Switch to GPT-4o fine-tuned model for patch generation
ai.summary: Patch generation now uses a fine-tuned `gpt-4o-2024-08-06` model instead of local diff expansion logic. The backend `generatePatch` function constructs a prompt with line-numbered file content and calls `promptOpenAI` with the specific model ID `ft:gpt-4o-2024-08-06:manifold-markets:run-1:A4VfZwvz`. This change affects `backend/src/generate-patch.ts`, `backend/src/openai-api.ts`, and `common/src/actions.ts`, where the `CHANGES` schema is updated to handle structured `FileChange` objects rather than raw patch strings. Timeout for OpenAI requests increased to 200 seconds in `backend/src/openai-api.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant now generates code changes through a new AI model instead of the old local logic. If you asked it to edit a file, you'll notice the generated edits now come tagged with line numbers and structured file-change objects rather than raw text patches, and edits take longer to finish because the model is allowed up to 200 seconds to respond. This switch is live today for all interactions that trigger patch generation.

The release also added two new test fixtures, which are sample codebases the assistant uses to practice handling Java and Python projects during automated checks. For you as a user, nothing in the assistant's behavior or features changes; these are quiet housekeeping updates that happen in the background to keep the system organized and ready for testing.

ai.title: Patch application uses hunk header line numbers
ai.summary: applyPatch parses @@ headers to seed context matching at startLineToTry before falling back to sequential oldIndex or trimmed matching. Covers common/src/util/patch.ts. Adds regex extraction for hunk start lines with 0-based index adjustment.

eli5.text: When you apply a set of edits to a document, the system now uses the line numbers listed at the start of each edit section to jump straight to the right spot, instead of always searching from the previous spot. If that number-based jump still fails to line up, it falls back to its old step-by-step search, so edits will still land even if the document changed slightly since the edit was written. The change also quiets some behind-the-scenes log messages that used to print while it was figuring all this out. You would only notice this if you are applying patches yourself; most people just see edits apply cleanly where they expect.

ai.summary: common/src/util/patch.ts now locates the first @@ hunk via findIndex instead of slicing a fixed 4-line header. This handles patches with variable header lengths. Internal utility change in Shared/Core.

eli5.text: When the assistant applies a text patch to update content, it now finds the first hunk marker dynamically instead of assuming a fixed header size. The change only affects how the internal patch tool works - you won't notice it directly, but patches with unusual headers will work correctly now.
